body:
**Labels:** P1 - High, Scope: MVP, Type: Bug, Type: UX

## Problem

The "SHOWING" value in the top data panel is inaccurate.

Observed behavior:

- Sometimes shows `0` even when cocktails are listed.
- Never shows a number larger than "YOU CAN MAKE".
- When "Show All Cocktails" is selected, SHOWING still caps at the "YOU CAN MAKE" value.
- The value does not consistently reflect what is actually rendered in the list.

This suggests SHOWING is being calculated from the wrong dataset or at the wrong lifecycle moment.

---

## Expected Behavior

SHOWING should always equal:

> The exact number of cocktails currently rendered in the UI list.

This includes all active filters:
- Mode (Show All / Can Make)
- Ingredient filtering
- Search filtering
- Approval filtering
- Any sorting or derived display logic

If 132 cocktails are rendered, SHOWING must display 132.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

- SHOWING always reflects the length of the rendered cocktail list.
- SHOWING updates correctly when:
  - Switching between "Show All" and "Can Make"
  - Adding/removing ingredients
  - Applying search filters
  - Toggling approval visibility
- No intermediate state shows incorrect 0 unless the rendered list is actually empty.
- Behavior verified manually in:
  - Show All mode
  - Can Make mode
  - With and without filters applied

---

## Implementation Notes

Likely root causes:

- SHOWING is computed from `canMakeCocktails` instead of the rendered list.
- SHOWING is calculated before async data load completes.
- SHOWING uses API count instead of the derived client-side display list.
- Separate lists are used for rendering vs counting.

Recommended fix:

- Derive SHOWING from the exact computed array used in the `v-for` rendering.
- Avoid storing SHOWING as mutable state.
- Prefer a computed property tied directly to the display list.

Example pattern:

```ts
const displayedCocktails = computed(() => {
  // full filtering + sorting pipeline
  return result;
});

const showingCount = computed(() => displayedCocktails.value.length);
title: SHOWING Count Incorrect in Top Data Panel

## Problem

User-submitted cocktails require:
- User visibility of their own submissions
- Admin approval workflow
- Clear status communication

These features are currently fragmented across separate issues.

---

## User Features (My Cocktails)

### Acceptance Criteria
- Navigation link: "My Cocktails"
- Shows cocktails where `CreatedByUserId == currentUserId`
- Displays status badge:
  - Approved
  - Pending
  - Rejected
- Sorted by newest first
- Unapproved cocktails hidden from public browse

---

## Admin Features (Moderation Queue)

### Acceptance Criteria
- Admin-only page showing pending cocktails
- Ability to:
  - Approve
  - Reject
- Rejected cocktails remain visible to submitter
- Approval metadata stored (`ApprovedUtc`, `ApprovedByUserId`)

---

## Notes

This consolidates submission lifecycle into a single coherent workflow.

**Labels:** P1 - High, Scope: MVP, Type: Enhancement

## Problem

Production contains:
- Duplicate cocktails
- Duplicate ingredients

Some ingredients are similar but not identical.

We need a controlled way to merge and clean data.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Admin-only maintenance endpoint or internal tool
- Supports:
  - Dry-run mode (reports suspected duplicates)
  - Apply mode (explicit merge operations)
- Ingredient merge operation:
  - Repoints `CocktailIngredients`
  - Repoints `UserIngredients`
  - Deletes or deactivates duplicate
- All operations logged

## Implementation Notes

- Start with exact/normalized name duplicates
- Add manual merge-by-id capability
- Avoid automatic destructive cleanup without explicit confirmation
title: Admin Maintenance Tool for Deduplication and Merge

body:
# Ingredient Normalization + Canonicalization Strategy

**Replaces:** #62  
**Closes:** #40  
**Labels:** P0 - Critical, Scope: MVP, Type: Core Feature, Type: Architecture

## Problem

We are creating duplicate Ingredients due to inconsistent naming (casing, spacing, wording).  

Additionally, we need a long-term canonical strategy for ingredient identity:
- "Whiskey" vs "Bourbon" vs "Rye"
- Brand vs base spirit
- Aliases and substitutions

Currently this leads to:
- Duplicate ingredient rows
- Messy joins
- Future substitution complexity

---

## Phase A (MVP – Critical)

### Goals
- Prevent duplicate Ingredients on creation (manual + import)
- Normalize names consistently

### Acceptance Criteria
- Add `NormalizedName` column to Ingredients
- Normalize on create:
  - Trim
  - Collapse whitespace
  - Lowercase
- Reuse existing ingredient if normalized match found
- Add unique index on `NormalizedName` (if feasible)
- Backfill normalized values for existing rows

---

## Phase B (Post-MVP – Strategic)

### Goals
- Canonical ingredient model
- Alias/substitution structure
- Category relationships (e.g., Bourbon ⊂ Whiskey)

### Potential Enhancements
- IngredientAliases table
- IngredientHierarchy table
- Substitution rules

---

## Notes

Phase A is required immediately to stop data corruption.  
Phase B defines the long-term data model.
title: Ingredient Normalization + Canonicalization Strategy

body:
We need an **Advanced Filters** UI pattern similar to shopping sites (Amazon sidebar), but **collapsed by default** so the main page stays clean.

The existing basic filters on the main page are correct and should NOT be expanded further. Any additional filtering logic belongs in this advanced pane.

This ticket is primarily about the collapsible pane setup and full reset behavior.

---

## Goals (MVP)

- Add an **Advanced Filters** pane that:
  - Slides in from the LEFT
  - Is collapsed by default
  - Does not clutter the main cocktail list UI
- Provide a prominent **Reset All** action that resets ALL filters (basic + advanced).

---

## UI / UX Requirements

### Entry Point
- Add an **“Advanced Filters”** button near existing filter controls.
- Clicking opens a LEFT-side drawer/pane.
- Drawer overlays or shifts content depending on layout (implementation choice).

### Pane Behavior
- Closed by default.
- Slide-in from LEFT.
- Closing the pane does NOT clear filters.
- Works cleanly on mobile (slide-over) and desktop.

### Reset Behavior
- Include a clear **Reset All Filters** action inside the pane.
- Reset All must:
  - Clear ALL filters (basic + advanced)
  - Restore global defaults (e.g., Popular-only default ON)
  - Refresh results immediately

---

## Advanced Filter Groups (inside pane)

These filters will live inside the Advanced pane:

- **My**
  - e.g., My Submissions / My Approved (definition TBD)
- **Cocktail Time Periods**
- **Source**
- **Flavor Profile**
- **Ingredients**
  - Show top ~15 most popular ingredients initially
  - Include **“See more”** expansion to reveal full list
  - Expansion should be inline (Amazon-style)

Notes:
- Ingredient list must be performant.
- Do not render thousands of checkboxes immediately.
- Advanced filters should integrate cleanly with existing filter pipeline.

---

## Functional Requirements

- Add a structured “advanced filter state” model separate from basic filters.
- Merge basic + advanced filter state into a single query pipeline.
- Maintain consistent persistence behavior with existing filter logic.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

- Advanced Filters button opens LEFT-side drawer.
- Drawer is collapsed by default.
- Reset All clears ALL filters and restores default state.
- Placeholder sections exist for each advanced filter group.
- Mobile + desktop layouts function correctly.
- Main cocktail list remains visually uncluttered.

---

## Labels

- `P2 - Medium`
- `Scope: Nice-to-Have`
- `Type: UX`
- `Type: Enhancement`
title: Add Left-Side Collapsible Advanced Filters Pane (Amazon-style) with Reset All

GROUPING FOR:

- Favorites
- Party lists
- Thematic lists
- etc

So right now there was already an idea for "linking" the same drinks from different sources.  These recipes will almost always be different.  So you have 2 Gin and Tonics, one from source 1 and another from source 2.  So, this would allow for the display of multiple recipes of the same type (either on the same page or maybe with tabs) and you could also filter by this.

But it occurred to me that it would be nice to group cocktails together for any reason.  You should be able to create your own groupings like "Favorites" or "Rye Whiskey Only" or "2026 Superbowl Party" (drinks you will be making at the party).  

Of course needs to be easy to add recipes to groups and then view or filter by them.
title: Cocktail Grouping Strategy

**Replaces:** #38  
**Closes:** #36  
**Labels:** P1 - High, Scope: MVP, Type: Core Feature, Type: UX

## Problem

Amounts need:
1. A consistent storage format (for logic and calculations)
2. A clean display format (Unicode fractions like ¼, ½, ¾)

Currently:
- Storage may be inconsistent
- Display formatting logic is fragmented

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### Storage
- Define canonical DB representation (decimal preferred)
- Preserve original textual input if needed
- Standardize units (oz, ml, dash, etc.)
- Migrate existing records if required

### Display
- Convert decimal values to friendly fractions:
  - 0.25 → ¼
  - 0.5 → ½
  - 0.75 → ¾
- Consistent formatting across:
  - Cocktail detail view
  - Print view
  - Future exports

---

## Implementation Notes

- Consider a small utility service for fraction formatting
- Keep storage independent of display representation
- Avoid storing display-only values in DB
title: Amount Storage + Display Formatting Strategy
